claim_verdicts.evidence: git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:docs/team/sprint-example.md, lines 12-18: header 'Việc | Người nhận | Ước lượng | Trạng thái cuối sprint'; rows: 'API POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel | Dev 1 | 3', 'Nút "Hủy đơn"... | Dev 2 | 3', 'Chặn hủy đơn đã thanh toán | Dev 1 | 2', 'Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy | Dev 3 | 2', 'Sửa lỗi tổng tiền sai ở đơn nhiều dòng | Dev 4 | 1'. 3+3+2+2+1 = 11.

Line 17: 'Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy | Dev 3 | 2 | Chưa xong, chuyển sprint sau'. Sprint review: 'Việc "Ngừng gửi thông báo" chưa xong nên không được trình diễn — chưa xong thì chưa tính, dù đã viết gần hết code.' Lesson §5 now matches: not counted as done, and 'the file does not say why it took longer' (true: no cause given).

git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:docs/team/kanban-board-example.md: column header is 'Việc cần làm | Đang làm (giới hạn 2) | Chờ review (giới hạn 2) | Xong'; no estimate column and no number next to any item anywhere in the file.

Consistent with Scrum Guide 2020 (WebFetch summary): 'The Developers who will be doing the work are responsible for the sizing.'; 'Selecting how much can be completed within a Sprint may be challenging... the more confident they will be in their Sprint forecasts.'; 'The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.' The Guide does not mandate numeric estimates. 'Sometimes wrong in both directions' follows from 'made before the work'. Accepted as opinion.

Premise verified in repo: kanban-board-example.md has WIP-limited columns 'Đang làm (giới hạn 2)', no estimate column, and 'Vì sao không có "sprint"': 'gom chúng vào một khối hai tuần sẽ làm chậm những việc cần sửa ngay'. The conclusion ('less need to size') is not in the file; accepted as opinion, correctly ledgered as such and hedged ('less need', not 'no need').

No pinned source addresses it: Scrum Guide 2020 (checked in round 1) says nothing about inflated estimates; repo files are silent. Ledgered as kind opinion; lesson §6 frames it as a symptom ('when estimates are turned into deadlines and people start giving larger numbers'), not a universal law. Non-blocking (not number/syntax). Also matches outline item 2 of management.l1.estimates-are-not-commitments.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, new in round 2, stated as a universal: some teams do estimate in hours or ideal days. What is supportable is only Sprint 14: its retro speaks of 'mỗi việc lớn hơn 3 điểm' (points), not hours. Next lesson's outline covers the general case.
issues.quote: The numbers a team gives compare stories with each other; they are not hours or days, and the next lesson shows how they are chosen.
issues.fix: Replace with: "The numbers in Sprint 14 compare items with each other; they are not hours or days, and the next lesson shows how they are chosen." Add to claims (kind fact, section 4, source docs/team/sprint-example.md retrospective line '3 điểm').

issues.text: Same unsupported planning narrative removed from §5 in round 1 survives in the suggested answer: sprint-example.md has no account of planning and does not say the estimates were used to choose the five items. Unlisted claim.
issues.quote: The estimate still did its job: it helped the team choose five items for two weeks.
issues.fix: Replace with: "An estimate like this still does its job: it helps a team judge how many items fit into a sprint."

issues.text: Summary line 5 asserts as fact what the file does not record (that the column was used to plan).
issues.quote: Sprint 14's `Ước lượng` column helped the team plan;
issues.fix: Replace with: "Sprint 14's `Ước lượng` column is the kind of number a team plans with;" and keep the rest of the line.

issues.text: q1 correct explanation still fixes a generic sprint at two weeks; §4 was changed to 'next sprint' in round 1 (Scrum Guide 2020: sprints are 'one month or less').
issues.quote: choose what fits into the next two weeks.
issues.fix: q1 explanation.en.correct: replace 'the next two weeks' with 'the next sprint'; vi: same change ('sprint tiếp theo').

issues.text: 'The review' is not defined anywhere I know. The only review in my vocabulary is code review, and a code review does not decide whether a sprint item counts as done. I cannot tell which meeting or person this is.
issues.quote: The review simply did not count it as done, and the file does not say why it took longer.
issues.fix: Replace 'The review' with words I know, e.g. 'At the end of the sprint, the team simply did not count it as done', or say in one clause that this is the meeting at the end of the sprint where finished work is shown.

issues.text: I never learn what the numbers 3, 3, 2, 2, 1 measure: days, hours, something else? The lesson adds them up (11) and the quiz asks me to take 'a similar amount' next sprint, but only the Connections line hints 'relative size, not hours'. I kept reading '3' as '3 days', which is exactly the deadline reading the lesson argues against.
issues.quote: after each one the team says a small number: 3, 3, 2, 2, 1.
issues.fix: Add one sentence in 'How it works' after 'compared with the others': the numbers compare stories with each other (a 2 is bigger than a 1), they are not hours or days, and how they are chosen is the next lesson.

issues.text: q3 option b says '11 points'. The lesson never calls the numbers 'points'; I don't know whether points are the same as the numbers in the `Ước lượng` column or a different unit.
issues.quote: Promise the product owner that exactly 11 points will be done
issues.fix: Replace 'exactly 11 points' with 'items adding up to exactly 11'.

issues.text: q4 correct option uses 'pad them'. The lesson says 'giving larger numbers to protect themselves', never 'pad'. As a Vietnamese reader I do not know this verb; I picked a by the rest of the sentence, not by understanding it.
issues.quote: Treating estimates as deadlines made people pad them, so they stopped helping planning
issues.fix: Replace 'made people pad them' with 'made people give larger numbers to protect themselves' (same words as section 6).

issues.text: The diagram's last arrow is dotted while all others are solid; the prose covers 'look back ... next estimates get better' but never says what the dotted line means compared with the solid ones.
issues.fix: Add a few words to the last sentence of section 4, e.g. '(the dashed arrow in the diagram)', or make the arrow solid.

issues.text: I had to re-read the first sentence of the third paragraph; 'What an estimate is not is ...' is hard to parse. The same paragraph then packs three ideas (not a promise; work without estimate; looking back).
issues.quote: What an estimate is not is a promise to someone outside the team.
issues.fix: Replace with 'An estimate is not a promise to someone outside the team.'

issues.text: q1, q2 and q5 correct options are near-verbatim sentences from the lesson (summary line 1; section 4 'uses only what is known'; section 5 'limits what is in progress instead'). q1 is also guessable: b, c, d are clearly unrelated.
issues.quote: The Kanban team limits work in progress instead of planning a batch, so it needs sizes less
issues.fix: Reword the correct options in different words from the lesson, e.g. q5: 'That team pulls one item at a time within its limits, so it rarely has to judge a whole sprint's worth of work up front'.

issues.text: q5 option c and its explanation talk about 'the support team' and items 'from a quick fix to an investigation'. This lesson only says 'that team' and never describes its items, so the explanation relies on facts I cannot check from the text.
issues.quote: Its items range from a quick fix to an investigation; they are not the same size.
issues.fix: Explanation c: 'Nothing in the lesson says the items are the same size; the reason given is the WIP limit, not the size.' Replace 'support team' in option c with 'Kanban team'.

issues.text: q4 wrong-option explanations use 'only when ... had changed', which reads oddly; I had to re-read b to see it means 'only if'.
issues.quote: This would explain it only when speed had changed
issues.fix: Replace 'only when' with 'only if' in q4 explanations b, c and d.

skipped_steps: What unit the estimate numbers use (3, 3, 2, 2, 1) is never stated, yet the lesson and quiz add them up.
